newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Industry package kills McDonnell's RAAF bid - source.
newsitem.headline: Industry package kills McDonnell's RAAF bid - source.

text.p: An insufficient package of Australian industry participation led to McDonnell Douglas's exclusion from an Australian jet trainer competition, a source close to the programme said on Friday.
"There was nothing wrong with it (the T-45)," said the source. "It is a fine aircraft. But the Australian participation (offered) was not enough."

Earlier, Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said the short-list for the Royal Australian Air Force requirement for up to 40 "lead-in fighters" had been reduced to the British Aerospace Hawk and Aermacchi SpA.
McDonnell Douglas's offer of the T-45 Goshawk, the heavily modified U.S. Navy version of the Hawk, had been eliminated, the minister said in a statement.
He added: "It is anticipated that Australian industry will play a major role in the assembly, test and ongoing support of the new aircraft."
British Aerospace's bid includes Australian assembly of some aircraft from parts supplied from Britain, and engine work to be performed by Qantas Airways Ltd.

The T-45's elimination means Rolls-Royce Plc will supply engines for the new aircraft. Both surviving bidders use Rolls-Royce engines: the Adour turbofan in the Hawk and the Viper turbojet in the MB.339.
The T-45's option of the AlliedSignal F124 engine as an alternative to the Adour had been seen as one of McDonnell Douglas's two main strengths in the competition.
The other was the T-45's suitability to training pilots for Australia's McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet fighters.
